title: Quadratic stsc lookup can cause denial of service during HEIF open
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (model not specified for this finding)
summary: Opening a file with a moov box used a linear search of stsc entries for every chunk, yielding quadratic work and seconds-to-minutes CPU use on files with many chunks. This issue was also independently reported as GHSA-xf84-wgwm-8vhx; the advisory explicitly says Anthropic OSS Scanner independently discovered the same issue.
ai_role: The item-level libheif advisory explicitly attributes discovery to Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-ZNJZAJWY. The release notes independently state that all listed security issues were found by the scanner. The Anthropic program sources establish model-based scanning, but no per-case model is identified.
classification_note: The primary advisory establishes a publicly disclosed security finding and direct Anthropic OSS Scanner attribution. No CVE had been assigned in the libheif release notes at the checked time; the distinct GHSA is used. No exploitation or zero-day status is asserted.
remediation_note: The lookup is now a binary search and malformed decreasing first_chunk values are rejected; fixed in libheif 1.23.7. The advisory also discloses OpenAI Codex assistance with the human reporter’s review and drafting; Anthropic discovery attribution is separately explicit. The libheif v1.23.7 security release is dated 2026-10-26; deployed patch status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: A crafted file can cause excessive CPU work during opening; concurrent requests can exhaust the media worker pool. Applies when untrusted inputs are processed by affected libheif usage.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.
